review.alternative: Improvements might arise from the scale of the base model rather than the collaborative framework itself.
review.would_change_mind: A comparative study showing no improvement between single-agent and multi-agent evolution under controlled compute budgets.

claims.statement: Autonomous multi-agent evolution frameworks (such as CORAL) enable agents to identify and solve novel research problems more effectively than fixed heuristic baselines by leveraging shared memory and agent communication.

support.explanation: This establishes a practical implementation for autonomous problem formulation beyond static rules.
support.passage: CORAL replaces rigid control with long-running agents that explore, reflect, and collaborate through shared persistent memory, asynchronous multi-agent execution, and heartbeat-based interventions.

review.alternative: Curiosity may simply be a heuristic that mimics exploration but lacks deep semantic grounding for true scientific discovery.
review.would_change_mind: Evidence that intrinsic motivation consistently leads to maladaptive behavior in open-ended task environments.

claims.statement: Curiosity-driven learning acts as a normative framework for enabling autonomous organisms to solve complex problems even when explicit rewards are deceptive or sparse.

support.explanation: This mechanism provides a foundational approach for agents to independently prioritize tasks when objective function signals are weak.
support.passage: We argue that curiosity-driven learning enables organisms to make discoveries to solve complex problems with rare or deceptive rewards.

actions.findings:
Autonomous multi-agent evolution frameworks (such as CORAL) enable agents to identify and solve novel research problems more effectively than fixed heuristic baselines by leveraging shared memory and agent communication. [source-91aafd52adc047b4]

Curiosity-driven learning acts as a normative framework for enabling autonomous organisms to solve complex problems even when explicit rewards are deceptive or sparse. [source-907e29b1da6b4646]
actions.limitations: Current implementation of autonomous evolution is restricted to task-specific domains; long-term longitudinal stability of curiosity-driven systems remains unverified.
actions.next_questions: How do these agents maintain goal alignment during multi-agent collaboration? Can curiosity mechanisms be scaled to non-algorithmic, real-world physical research tasks?
actions.reason: Incorporating recent findings on autonomous agent evolution (CORAL) to deepen the mechanical understanding of autonomous problem formulation.
actions.summary: Autonomous discovery in artificial agents can be achieved by moving beyond fixed heuristics toward multi-agent frameworks that facilitate shared persistent memory, reflection, and evolution. Curiosity and intrinsic motivation, traditionally conceptualized as developmental mechanisms in biological organisms, are now being implemented as algorithmic drivers for open-ended research.

proposal.summary: Revised inquiry into autonomous research problem formulation, incorporating new multi-agent evolution frameworks as mechanisms for open-ended discovery.

review.alternative: Implicitly distributed reasoning in monolithic prompts may offer better latent performance at the cost of interpretability.
review.would_change_mind: Evidence that monolithic models consistently outperform decoupled agents on justification tasks without auxiliary memory.

claims.statement: Architectural separation of cognition, control, and memory can make the justificatory basis of AI decisions explicit.

support.explanation: This separation allows the system to treat the 'control' (governing axioms) as a discrete, inspectable entity rather than an opaque part of the cognition prompt.
support.passage: The Structured Cognitive Loop (SCL) is introduced as an architectural alternative that separates these functions. In SCL, the language model is dedicated to cognition only, execution is governed by a lightweight controller that mediates every proposal before any action is taken, and memory is maintained externally as a structured store of verified facts.

review.alternative: Self-correction limitations are due to insufficient scale rather than fundamental methodology.
review.would_change_mind: Evidence of smaller models achieving robust self-correction without external teacher-model supervision.

claims.statement: Teacher-guided supervision overcomes the inherent limitations of solo self-correction in smaller models.

support.explanation: SuperCorrect demonstrates that 'correcting' a model's logic requires an external validation process, supporting the idea that models struggle with identifying their own foundational reasoning errors independently.
support.passage: To overcome these limitations, we propose SuperCorrect, a novel two-stage framework that uses a large teacher model to supervise and correct both the reasoning and reflection processes of a smaller student model.

actions.findings:
Architectural separation of cognition, control, and memory can make the justificatory basis of AI decisions explicit. [source-51196608d740480b]

Teacher-guided supervision overcomes the inherent limitations of solo self-correction in smaller models. [source-90a697b24b434444]
actions.limitations: Current methods like SCL and SuperCorrect externalize control or supervision, meaning the 'identification' of axioms is still largely engineered by the designer rather than autonomously generated by the model.
actions.next_questions: Can these frameworks be adapted to allow the system to flag its own logical constraints as revisable hypotheses rather than fixed architectural parameters?
actions.reason: Incorporating findings on SCL and SuperCorrect to address the project goal of identifying and challenging foundational assumptions.
actions.summary: Recent advances indicate that foundational reasoning axioms are best challenged through architectural separation (separating justification from cognition) and structured, teacher-guided self-correction, rather than relying on unguided self-reflection.
actions.title: Architectural and Methodological Paths to Reasoning Transparency
